documents.unit: THEE Pathway (General Education) common syllabus links
documents.title: Common Syllabus Links for Students: AI Policy
documents.stance_why: The policy says "AI use is permissible when used for specific tasks as noted and approved by the course instructor" and lists approved uses "with instructor approval", so AI is allowed only when the instructor approves; it also says "individual faculty, departments, and/or colleges may have additional criteria", leaving the decision to instructors, with no tiers or templates. It reads as delegates, with a floor that graded work cannot be fully AI-created and must be cited.
documents.summary: The AI Policy section of Jackson State's common syllabus statements treats generative AI as a possible aid to learning that instructors approve for specific tasks. It lists approved uses, bars fully AI-created graded work, requires citation, and prohibits entering protected personal data into AI. Misuse and uncited use count as academic dishonesty.

units.why: The opening says AI "can be a useful tool that can accelerate learning", a statement of purpose and principle for the university-wide policy; fits the institution-wide framework type rather than a rationale type because it frames the whole policy.
units.anchor: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be a useful tool that can accelerate learning.

units.why: States the policy "may adjust based on this evolution", i.e. it is provisional and will change; P54 fits (revisit policy), though the adjusting is at the instructor's discretion.
units.anchor: this policy may adjust based on this evolution at the course instructor’s discretion

units.why: "individual faculty, departments, and/or colleges may have additional criteria" lets lower units add rules so long as they do not conflict; this is about who sets rules beyond the university text, so P04 (decision by instructor/unit) rather than P09.
units.anchor: individual faculty, departments, and/or colleges may have additional criteria in their syllabus for using AI
units.frag_start: Please be advised that individual faculty
units.frag_end: does not conflict with this policy.

units.why: "supplement student learning, not to replace human creativity, ingenuity, or critical thinking" says AI must not replace students' thinking; P32 (student stays primary thinker) fits better than the general rationale types.
units.anchor: to supplement student learning, not to replace human creativity, ingenuity, or critical thinking
units.frag_start: The goal of integrating AI in education

units.why: "AI use is permissible when used for specific tasks as noted and approved by the course instructor" sets a default: allowed only for instructor-approved tasks, i.e. restrict; P04 fits as the instructor decides, and P01/P02 do not since this is neither a ban nor free permission.
units.anchor: AI use is permissible when used for specific tasks as noted and approved

units.why: Lists "to help brainstorm assignments, presentations, design ideation" as an approved use with instructor approval; brainstorming type P15.
units.anchor: to help brainstorm assignments, presentations, design ideation, etc.

units.why: Permits AI "to create a plan, outline and generate examples for assignments" with approval; closest to exploring approaches (P15) since it is planning help, not submitted work.
units.anchor: to create a plan, outline and generate examples for assignments

units.why: Permits AI "to summarize or synthesize sources to enhance understanding"; understanding-oriented use like a tutor, P12 (P14 study aids is a weaker fit since it is about sources for assignments).
units.anchor: to summarize or synthesize sources to enhance understanding

units.why: Permits using AI "to learn prompt engineering", i.e. learning to use AI as a skill; P44 (effective AI use as skill).
units.anchor: to learn prompt engineering; crafting precise inputs (prompts) to guide AI models

units.why: Permits AI "to assist in finding, analyzing, and researching sources" with approval; not a prose or code rule, so closest is tutor/understanding use P12.
units.anchor: to assist in finding, analyzing, and researching sources

units.why: Permits AI "to help understand different perspectives or viewpoints"; understanding concepts, P12.
units.anchor: to help understand different perspectives or viewpoints

units.why: Permits AI "to enhance, improve, edit or revise their own original work" including written work; prose/editing rule, P18 (P21 is the prohibition type and does not fit).
units.anchor: to enhance, improve, edit or revise their own original work
units.frag_start: to enhance, improve, edit or revise

units.why: Warns AI "may also be flawed" so outputs are not reliable; the verify-output type P31, stated as a caveat on the permitted uses.
units.anchor: a variety of outputs that may be helpful but may also be flawed
units.frag_start: These options are with the understanding

units.why: "no final assignment, presentation, paper, or other graded work can be fully created by AI" bars submitting AI-produced work, with an exception where AI use is the assignment; P19.
units.anchor: no final assignment, presentation, paper, or other graded work can be fully created by AI

units.why: "will receive a zero for that specific assignment" states a concrete penalty, at instructor discretion; P37 rather than P36 since the content is the sanction.
units.anchor: fully created by AI will receive a zero for that specific assignment
units.frag_start: At the instructor’s discretion, any assignments

units.why: "The unauthorized use of AI is a form of academic dishonesty" classifies misuse as misconduct; P36.
units.anchor: The unauthorized use of AI is a form of academic dishonesty.

units.why: "the submitted work must cite such usage properly" requires citing any AI use in graded work in a standard style; P24 (disclosure); P25 not chosen because no tool/prompt details are demanded.
units.anchor: the submitted work must cite such usage properly in accordance with current citation
units.frag_start: If AI is utilized for any graded work,

units.why: "The use of AI without proper citation is also a form of academic dishonesty" makes nondisclosure itself the violation; P28 fits better than P36 because it is specifically about failing to cite.
units.anchor: The use of AI without proper citation is also a form of academic dishonesty.

units.why: "Guidance and examples of AI citations from the main three style manuals are below" points students to APA, MLA and Chicago guidance on citing AI; supports the citation requirement, coded as P24 since it supplies how to cite, with no tool/prompt demand.
units.anchor: Guidance and examples of AI citations from the main three style manuals are below.

units.why: "prohibited from inputting any personal, sensitive, or otherwise confidential information" into any AI program protects protected data; P50 (data protection), covering all JSU community members.
units.anchor: prohibited from inputting any personal, sensitive, or otherwise confidential information
units.frag_start: Members of the JSU community are prohibited

notes: Only the AI Policy paragraph of the common syllabus page was coded; the Academic Honesty text above it does not mention AI and was skipped.
